trust_decision.summary: An untrusted request path (or Googlebot _escaped_fragment_ query) is matched against route regexes built from developer route templates with lazy [^/]*? parameter groups and no match timeout; the matcher decides how much CPU an attacker-chosen URL may consume.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'ReDoS in routing'; DotvvmRoute.IsMatch is the only place a route regex is executed against the request URL.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any DotVVM page request: DotvvmRoutingMiddleware.Handle -> DotvvmRoute.IsMatch uses the regex built here (also LocalizedDotvvmRoute, AddUrlRedirection/AddRouteRedirection, AddGroup, resource route)
HTTP request to any URL handled by DotVVM (routing middleware, local resource middleware); public API RouteBase.IsMatch
HTTP request through DotvvmRoutingMiddleware.Handle (timeout mapped to 503)
build: adds net8.0 TFM so the #if NET7_0_OR_GREATER NonBacktracking fallback in DotvvmRoute.IsMatch is compiled (fix.diff:13-16)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/Framework/Framework/Hosting/Middlewares/DotvvmRoutingMiddleware.cs:101 (timeout->503 wrapper, fix.diff:2293-2310); plus src/Directory.Build.props:28-29 (net8 TFM needed for the NonBacktracking fallback to exist)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once a match timeout is set in the parser, the middleware catch and the TFM change look like cosmetics/infra ('the timeout already bounds CPU'), and the NonBacktracking path looks unreachable at the pinned TFMs (netstandard2.1;net6.0).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Developer-supplied regex(...) route constraints are spliced verbatim into the route regex, and the resource route uses regex(.*); forcing RegexOptions.NonBacktracking or a URL/segment length cap globally would reject constructs NonBacktracking does not support or break long legitimate resource/slug URLs, and lazy param capture semantics must stay identical.

required, optional (?), constrained and adjacent parameters in route templates — src/Framework/Framework/Routing/DotvvmRouteParser.cs:177-182 (tests at fix.diff:788-940)

O7_producer.where: src/Framework/Framework/Routing/DotvvmRouteParser.cs:78-85 builds the route regex at route registration; DotvvmRoute stores it at src/Framework/Framework/Routing/DotvvmRoute.cs:80

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Resource URL matcher using its own Regex (instead of a DotvvmRoute) built without a timeout, reached via DotvvmLocalResourceMiddleware before routing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Resource serving is a separate middleware (src/Framework/Framework/Hosting/Middlewares/DotvvmLocalResourceMiddleware.cs:27) with a fixed route template; a maintainer optimising it could plausibly inline a hand-written Regex, a true second implementation at distance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IsPartialMatch loop that matches culture routes with a separately compiled regex (e.g. culture-prefix regex) outside DotvvmRoute.IsMatch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Partial matching already iterates all localized routes per request outside the exact-match path; a culture-prefix regex there is a natural feature addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Routes deserialized from configuration JSON compiled by a separate code path that does not go through DotvvmRouteParser.ParseRouteUrl.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Config-loader route production is a save/reload boundary a solver checking only the parser would not inspect.

O9_family: ReDoS / uncontrolled regex backtracking (CWE-1333) in URL route matching
